card_summary: Vizrt launched AI-powered advances for media management. The company introduced new features to improve speed and accuracy in live production. Vizrt's new features will impact live signal transport with potential for reduced latency and improved signal integrity, aligning with ST 2110 and NMOS standards for real-time transport and frame-accuracy.

Technical Analysis: Vizrt Integrates JPEG XS for Low-Latency Graphics Transport in Live Productions

Vizrt has announced the integration of JPEG XS compression into their graphics workflow, enabling low-latency and high-quality video transport for live productions. This development involves the use of JPEG XS, a compression standard that allows for visually lossless video transport at low bitrates, making it suitable for live broadcast applications. The integration is expected to improve the efficiency of live graphics workflows, particularly in scenarios where high-quality video and low latency are crucial.

Operational ROI

The integration of JPEG XS into Vizrt's graphics workflow is expected to save broadcast CTOs significant costs and time by reducing the bitrate required for transporting high-quality video. For instance, JPEG XS can achieve visually lossless compression at bitrates as low as 100 Mbps, compared to uncompressed 12G-SDI, which requires a much higher bitrate. This reduction in bitrate can lead to lower transmission costs and simplified signal routing, particularly in live production scenarios where multiple video feeds need to be transported over long distances. The workflow step most affected by this development is the transport of live graphics and video feeds from the studio to the broadcast center or other remote locations.

In comparison to existing approaches, such as using uncompressed 12G-SDI or other compression standards like H.264, the use of JPEG XS offers a significant reduction in latency and an improvement in video quality. Uncompressed 12G-SDI, for example, requires a much higher bitrate and can be more prone to signal degradation over long distances, whereas JPEG XS provides a more efficient and reliable means of transporting high-quality video. This change operationally simplifies the setup and configuration of live production workflows, as broadcast engineers can now rely on a single, standardized compression format for all their video transport needs.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS into Vizrt's graphics workflow is designed to fit seamlessly into existing broadcast IT stacks, with support for relevant standards and protocols such as ST 2110, NMOS, and AES67. From a cybersecurity perspective, the use of JPEG XS compression does not introduce any new vulnerabilities, as it is a standardized compression format that has been extensively tested and validated by the industry. Broadcasters can also rely on existing security measures, such as encryption and access control, to protect their video feeds during transport. Additionally, the use of JPEG XS is compliant with relevant standards and regulations, such as SMPTE ST 2110-22, which defines the use of JPEG XS compression for professional media applications.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: To deploy JPEG XS compression in a live production workflow, broadcast engineers will need to ensure that their equipment and infrastructure support the standard, including compatible video interfaces, such as 12G-SDI, and sufficient network bandwidth to handle the compressed video feeds.
  • Compatibility: The integration of JPEG XS into Vizrt's graphics workflow is compliant with relevant standards and protocols, including SMPTE ST 2110-20, NMOS IS-04, and AES67, ensuring seamless integration with existing broadcast systems and equipment.
  • What to Watch: Broadcast engineers should track the upcoming updates to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new specifications for the use of JPEG XS compression in live production workflows, as well as the development of new equipment and systems that support the standard.

The integration of JPEG XS into Vizrt's graphics workflow signals a significant shift towards more efficient and reliable video transport in live productions, and broadcast engineers should take note of the potential benefits and requirements of deploying this technology in their own workflows. As the industry continues to adopt JPEG XS compression, engineers should stay informed about the latest developments and updates to the standard to ensure they can take full advantage of its capabilities.

Analysis: Vizrt's AI-powered media management supports ST 2110, enabling efficient IP-based workflows with reduced latency and optimized bitrate for live broadcast and streaming applications.
